 NBA Fantasy: Week 5 fantasy rookie power rankings
 Updated rookie power rankings from a fantasy perspective in Week 5 of the NBA season.
 Steve Inman & Jed Katz, NBA.com
 November 17, 2026 4:12 PM In three games last week, Darius Acuff Jr. averaged 24 points, six assists and 1.3 steals for the Sacramento Kings. 
 Play Yahoo Fantasy High Score Today! 
 The 2026 rookie class has continued to put up major numbers through the first few weeks of the season. Nine players from the 2026 NBA Draft class are averaging double-digit scoring, making them extremely appealing for fantasy managers. 
 Caleb Wilson suffered a fractured right hand and will miss multiple weeks after undergoing surgery, which has significant implications on our Rookie Fantasy Power Rankings. Check out Week 5’s top 10. 
 10. Christian Anderson , Charlotte Hornets
 Last Week: NR↑ 
 The last four games have only given more opportunities to Anderson, who received sparing minutes in his first eight appearances. Across those four contests, the 18th overall pick is averaging 10.5 points and 2.5 assists in 19.3 minutes. If Charlotte continues to put Anderson on the floor, these numbers could take even more of a leap, which should intrigue fantasy managers in deeper leagues. 
 9. Brayden Burries , Milwaukee Bucks
 Last Week: 7↓ 
 Burries has been a full-time starter in Milwaukee since early November, and while the last four games haven’t been great for him in the efficiency department (30.8% shooting), the floor is higher than most if he’s in the Bucks’ first five. Burries is still making an impact on the glass and as a facilitator. Over Milwaukee’s last four games, he’s averaged five rebounds, 2.8 assists and one steal. 
 8. Keaton Wagler , LA Clippers
 Last Week: 9↑ 
 Wagler has found some consistency over the last five games. From Nov. 4 onward, he’s averaging 12.6 points, three assists and one steal on extremely impressive 46/46/90 shooting splits. The fifth overall pick is still coming off the bench, but he’s a firm sixth man for them at 23.1 minutes. If the Clippers decide to make lineup changes, Wagler could certainly get bumped into the starting five if this scoring efficiency holds. 
 7. Aday Mara , Oklahoma City Thunder
 Last Week: 10↑ 
 Mara’s play is starting to pick up with an increase in minutes. Over the last seven days (four games), the 12th overall pick averaged 11.8 points, eight rebounds and 1.3 blocks. In that span he put up two double-doubles and averaged 26.2 minutes. With Chet Holmgren still out a while with his injury, Mara is taking control of the center minutes in Oklahoma City. 
 6. Meleek Thomas , Cleveland Cavaliers
 Last Week: 8↑ 
 The Cavaliers trust Thomas to be a spark plug off the bench. The 34th overall pick is firmly within their rotation, averaging 13.3 points, 2.9 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.2 steals this season. What makes the former Arkansas standout special is his movement on both ends of the floor. Thomas is an active defender with a near-6-foot-7 wingspan, but can also score on and off the ball (limited sample size) from plenty of areas. Thomas’ busiest spot is above the break, with 42 attempts. Overall, he’s shooting 47% from the field and 42.3% from 3-point range. 
 5. AJ Dybantsa , Washington Wizards
 Last Week: 5 
 Dybantsa struggled with his efficiency this week, shooting just 35.6% from the field over the last week. The encouraging part about his performance is that his scoring struggles didn’t stop him from continuing to shoot. Dybantsa averaged 14.8 shot attempts in his four matchups this week, right around his season average (14.2). After missing his first four games of the season due to injury, Dybantsa got off to a hot start in Washington. With all of these players being rookies, there are going to be ups and downs, especially as they get adjusted to the rigors of the NBA schedule. There is no cause for concern with Dybantsa and brighter days are ahead. 
 4. Darryn Peterson , Utah Jazz
 Last Week: 6↑ 
 Over the last week, Peterson’s fantasy outlook has improved significantly. In his four games over the last seven days, he averaged 23 points, five rebounds, 3.8 assists and 1.3 steals. In what started as a very crowded rotation in Utah, Peterson is one of the last Jazz starters from opening night standing. With Lauri Markkanen, Jaren Jackson Jr. and Jaxson Hayes all out, Peterson averaged 33 minutes and 19.5 shot attempts over the last week. If he continues this impressive play as expected, he could move up even higher in our Fantasy Rookie Power Rankings next week. 
 3. Cameron Boozer , Memphis Grizzlies
 Last Week: 4↑ 
 Boozer has been the most consistent rookie through the first four weeks of the NBA season and there was certainly discussion at NBA Fantasy HQ on putting him higher than No. 3 on the list this week. The third overall pick averaged 17.3 points, nine rebounds, five assists and 2.3 stocks per game over the last week. He also shot 46.4% from the field over those seven days, an improvement on his season stat of 39.3%. He hasn’t had the highs of Darius Acuff Jr. yet, but when all is said and done, he may end up with the best fantasy season among all the rookies. 
 2. Yaxel Lendeborg , Golden State Warriors
 Last Week:  2 
 Outside a 3-point game against the Spurs on Nov. 13, it has been more of the same for Lendeborg, who continues to make a strong case to be the Kia Rookie of the Year. He most recently dropped 28 points, 8 rebounds, 3 assists and 3 stocks against the Pelicans, and despite the loss, Golden State is 8-6 on the season, largely due to him stepping up as the next scoring option to Stephen Curry. Lendeborg’s vast experience at the collegiate level has allowed him to make an immediate impact on a Warriors team that has been searching for answers. His do-it-all play style has them sitting 11th in offensive rating and 13th in defensive rating. 
 1. Darius Acuff Jr. , Sacramento Kings
 Last Week: 1 
 The battle for No. 1 got even closer this week, but Acuff’s impressive first month of NBA action allowed him to hang on to the top position. Many of the best rookies have already emerged as top options offensively on their team. Acuff has certainly become that in Sacramento, as he leads all rookies and is tied for first in the entire NBA for minutes (36.8). In three games over the last week, Acuff averaged 24 points, six assists and 1.3 steals. He has attempted at least 20 shots in 12 of his 13 games this season. The only contest he did not, Nov. 13 against Portland, he attempted 19 shots. It continues to be the Acuff show in Sacramento, much to the delight of his fantasy managers.
